settings.description: The address and port Keystone listens on. The default is reachable from this machine only.
Whether the session cookie is marked for HTTPS only. Turn it on once Keystone is reached over HTTPS. A request that arrives over HTTPS gets the mark whatever this says.
The most bytes the API reads from one request's body. A larger body is refused.
How often an open stream sends a line that means only that it is still there, so nothing between Keystone and the browser closes a quiet connection.
The most rows a list in the API returns in one call. A client reads further pages to get the rest.
Whether the API tells someone who has not signed in the names of the people on this install, so the sign-in screen can ask who is signing in. Off, a person must know their own id.

How many rounds of PBKDF2-SHA-256 a password goes through before it is stored. More rounds make a stolen database slower to guess from. A stored password moves to the new count the next time its person signs in.
The fewest characters a new password may have.
How long a sign-in lasts before the person must sign in again.
How many wrong passwords in a row are taken before password sign-in makes the person wait.
How long password sign-in is refused after too many wrong passwords in a row.
Whether people may add passkeys and sign in with them. Off until the sign-in screen has proven them in a browser.
The host name passkeys are bound to, which must be the host people reach Keystone by. Changing it makes every stored passkey unusable.
The address in the browser's bar when a passkey is used: scheme, host and port. A passkey answer from any other page is refused.
How long a person has to answer a passkey prompt before it must be asked again.
The folder that holds keystone.json and one folder for each tenant.

Where a new install keeps the master key that protects every tenant's secrets. system is the operating system's key store: DPAPI on Windows, the login keychain on macOS, the Secret Service on Linux. file is a key file in the user's profile, for a machine with no key store, and is weaker. Once an install has stored a secret, keystone.json records the keeper and this setting is no longer read.
